faqs.a:
(a)
Controlled cross-connection required.
Each customer shall ensure that any cross-connection on the customer's property is
               controlled with an appropriate assembly or method as designated in this article. If
               the city becomes aware of a single-family residential connection to the public water
               system that is a cross-connection, the city will determine the type of backflow prevention
               assembly or backflow prevention method to control the cross-connection. The city will
               notify the customer of this determination, and the customer must install this type
               of assembly or method.
(b)
Appropriate device or method.
Each customer shall ensure that each assembly, method, or non-testable device located
               on the customer's property is appropriate for the identified contaminant at the cross-connection
               as set forth in the following table:
Table 102-276(b)
Appropriate Backflow Prevention Assemblies, Methods, or Non-testable Devices
Assembly or Method Type
Typical Appropriate Uses
Reduced Pressure Zone
Backflow Prevention Assembly ("RPZ")
Appropriate for any identified contaminant except direct connections to sewer or installations
                                 which may impair the integrity of the assembly to function as designed.
Reduced Pressure Zone Fire Protection Backflow
Prevention Assembly ("RPF")
Appropriate for cross connections to fire suppression systems.
Reduced Pressure Zone Detector Fire Protection Backflow Prevention Assembly ("RPD")
Double Check Backflow
Prevention Assembly ("DC")
Appropriate for cross-connections to fire suppression systems except when upstream
                                 of a chemical other than food grade glycerin.
Double Check Fire Protection Backflow Prevention
Assembly ("DCF")
Double Check Detector Fire Protection Backflow Prevention Assembly ("DCD")
Pressure Vacuum Breaker
Backflow Prevention Assembly ("PVB")*
Appropriate for any identified contaminant except direct connections to sewer or installations
                                 which may impair the integrity of the assembly to function as designed. Not appropriate
                                 for connections subject to backpressure.
Spill-Resistant Vacuum Breaker ("SVB")*
Air Gap ("AG")*
Appropriate for any identified contaminant. All cross-connections can be controlled
                                 using an air gap installed in accordance with standard ASME A112.1.1.
Block and Bleed Valve or Double Block and Bleed Valve ("BB")*
Appropriate for membrane chemical-clean-in-place and filter-to-waste at supplier's
                                 facilities.
Check Valve ("CV")*
The director shall have discretion as to whether these methods are appropriate.
Hydraulic Conditions ("HC")*
(c)
Installation to comply with applicable code.
The installation of each assembly or method shall comply with the International Plumbing
               Code, technical requirements, specifications, or other applicable standards, or any
               rule or regulation established by the director. Each assembly or method used is subject
               to the approval of the director. An assembly or method type marked with an asterisk
               in Table 102-276(b) requires the written approval of the director prior to installation.
               A customer may submit to the director a request to install an alternate assembly.
               The submission must be in writing, and must outline the exact nature of the alternate
               assembly, and detail with specificity the reason or reasons why the alternate assembly
               will provide the same or greater level of protection against backflow or backflow
               events as the assembly required under Table 102-276(b). Upon receipt of such a request
               by a customer, the director may, but is not required to, stay or defer any enforcement
               or other action authorized by this article based on the nature and potential severity
               of the risk presented by the delay.
(1)
Proper clearance required.
The customer must maintain the required clearance around the backflow prevention
               assembly to allow for testing and maintenance.
(d)
Other.
Each customer shall ensure that any backflow prevention assembly or method on the
               customer's property is inspected, tested, maintained, and is properly repaired or
               replaced as necessary.
(1)
Repair.
Each customer shall ensure each backflow prevention assembly or method located on
               the customer's property is repaired and retested or replaced as necessary whenever
               the assembly or method is found to be defective.
(2)
Records.
Each customer shall keep records and reports of inspections, tests, repairs, retests,
               and replacements for a minimum of three years.
(3)
Costs.
All costs related to the design, submittal, installation, inspection, re-inspection,
               maintenance, testing, repairs, and replacement related to backflow prevention assemblies
               and methods shall be borne by the customer.
(e)
Annual inspection report required; annual inspection due date; duties.
Following the initial installation, each customer shall, on or before July 31 of
               each subsequent year, test any backflow prevention assembly or method on the customer's
               property in accordance with this article, and submit to the director the annual inspection
               report.
(f)
Responsibilities in an uncontrolled cross-connection compliance action.
If a customer is ordered by the director to install at the customer's water service
               connection an approved backflow prevention assembly or method, or to take any other
               action to ensure the installation is completed in accordance with the requirements
               of this article, the installation or other action shall be completed by the customer
               and a completed inspection report submitted to the director within the time frame
               noted in the director's notice and order, unless the customer requests and the director
               issues a written extension of that time.
(g)
Duty to obey.
Each customer shall comply with any order of the director issued under this article,
               including an order to allow access to and entry into any structure, property, or premises
               for the purposes outlined in this article. Each customer shall cooperate with the
               survey process, and with the installation, inspection, testing, maintenance, repair,
               and replacement of backflow prevention assemblies.
(
Ord. No. 4829
, § 1, 12-5-2022)
